Alex / Priya — thanks again for a great discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same playbook.

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary use: customer support assistant + semantic search over policy docs (embeddings + reranker).
- Latency budget: 200ms P95 for interactive chat flows; asynchronous search can be higher.
- Auth: prefer short-lived API keys or mTLS for backend calls; SSO + RBAC for console.
- Observability: must be able to correlate requests with our distributed tracing (trace IDs), see per-request latency breakdown (batching, model, KV cache), and expose request-level metadata to your logging platform.

Open action items / asks from FinTechCo:
1) SDK integration checklist for Node + Python with recommended auth patterns.
2) Sample request/response snippets showing trace headers and latency breakdown in responses.
3) Guidance on structured output / tool calling for safe action execution and reranker integration for search results.
4) Sandbox credentials + timeline for a quick engineering pairing session.

Our proposed immediate next steps:
- Rishi / Monica will share an SDK checklist + observability hooks doc (by Monday).
- Engineering pairing session: 30–45 minutes with your engineers to walk through SDK setup and auth (Tues/Wed).
- We'll provide a sandbox project with example embeddings pipeline and a reranker recipe.

Please reply with which time windows work for the pairing session and any follow-up questions.

— Marissa

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few quick answers and follow-ups from our side:

Answers:
- We will likely do backend-to-backend calls (server-side) to avoid exposing keys in clients. mTLS is preferred for production; short-lived API keys okay for prototype.
- Embeddings: we plan to batch embed ingestion nightly (~100k docs) and use embeddings + a learned reranker for top-10 re-ranking.
- Latency: 200ms P95 target for the assistant; for reranker we can tolerate ~300–400ms in initial phase.

Questions:
1) Can you show a minimal curl example that propagates our internal trace id and surfaces Redwood latency breakdown headers in the response? (we use X-Request-ID currently)
2) For structured output/tool-calling: do you provide a schema validation step on your side or do you recommend validating client-side? Any recommended patterns for safe tool invocation?
3) For embeddings + reranker: do you offer a single endpoint that returns both embeddings and reranking scores or is that a two-step flow?

Alex — great questions. Short answers up front, then minimal examples.

1) Trace propagation + latency headers: yes. We recommend passing your X-Request-ID (or X-Trace-Id) into the Redwood call; we will echo it back and also include an X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown header. Example (curl):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.infer/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -H "X-Trace-Id: 6f72b3a4-9f2a-4d1a-8b9e-3a7e9c1d2f6b"
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3.1","input":"Summarize customer policy...","trace":true}'

Response headers will include: X-Redwood-Trace-Id (unique per backend span), X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: "kv_cache:5,batching:2,model:40" (values in ms). We also return a JSON body field trace:{"trace_id":"...","spans":[...]} if you set trace=true.

2) Structured output / tool calling: we support a structured "tools" object in responses and optional schema enforcement. Recommended pattern: 1) model proposes an action in a structured tools block, 2) your service validates the payload against your schema (we can provide optional server-side schema validation as a managed feature), 3) execute the tool call from your trusted backend and return execution result back into the chat context. We do not execute customer-side tools for safety reasons — all tool execution should be performed in your environment.

3) Embeddings + reranker: typically a two-step flow. You can call the embeddings endpoint for vectorization and then call the reranker endpoint with candidate IDs to get re-ranking scores. For many customers we provide a convenience "semantic_search" endpoint that performs retrieval + optional rerank in one call (configurable).

I'll get Monica to share a compact SDK checklist and an observability-hooks doc with sample response payloads and header examples. We can do Tues 2026-05-12 at 15:30 UTC for the pairing session; please confirm.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Observability hooks + SDK checklist (attachments)

Alex / Priya — attaching the observability hooks doc and a short SDK integration checklist (PDF). Key excerpts below to make integration easier:

Recommended headers (propagation):
- X-Request-ID: your existing request id (we echo back in X-Redwood-Echoed-Request-Id)
- X-Trace-Id: top-level trace id (we correlate to internal spans)
- X-User-Id: optional, if you want per-user metrics (PII guidance: send hashed id)

Response headers we expose:
- X-Redwood-Trace-Id: unique Redwood span id
- X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: comma-separated ms (e.g., "kv_cache:5,batching:2,model:40")
- X-Redwood-Cache-Hit: "true" or "false"

Response body (streaming-friendly) example snippet: 
{
  "id":"resp_abc123",
  "output":"...",
  "tools": [
    {"name":"get_account_balance","args":{"account_id":"123"},"confidence":0.87}
  ],
  "trace": {"trace_id":"6f72b3a4-9f2a-4d1a-8b9e-3a7e9c1d2f6b","spans": [{"name":"kv_lookup","dur_ms":5}] }
}

Observability best practices:
- Propagate your trace id (X-Trace-Id) into Redwood requests so logs in your system can be correlated with Redwood trace ids.
- Use the X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown header to populate a per-request metric and to drive dashboard panels (model vs batching vs cache).
- For streaming scenarios, include a small final JSON frame with the final tool call decisions and trace info for reliable attribution.

Embedding + reranker patterns:
- Ingest: batch embeddings job with per-document metadata (doc_id, chunk_id, source).
- Retrieval: semantic_search endpoint for coarse retrieval; call reranker with top-K candidate ids for scored ordering.
- Monitoring: track top-K recall and average rerank delta; Redwood can emit per-query reranker latency metrics to your Console (we can send a webhook or you can pull via API).

Attachments included: observability-hooks.md (detailed header examples and sample dashboards), sdk-integration-checklist.pdf (Node/Python snippets, auth patterns, tests).

I'll share a sandbox link and temporary API key in a separate secure message. See the quickstart gist in the links above.
